title: scenario
description: One recorded run of a trigger: the seed and generated input, the stubbed results of every effectful node, and the report the run produced. wilanis fuzz writes them; wilanis regress replays them and diffs node by node.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/scenario.schema.json.

description.description: What this scenario covers, in one or two sentences, so a reader knows why the recording is kept.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

generated.description: The command that wrote this scenario. A generated scenario is regenerated by that command and never edited: `wilanis rehearse --check` exits 1 when a file under `scenarios/rehearsed/` is stale, missing or extra against what the tree yields today. Absent: written by hand, kept as it is.

trigger.description: The trigger this run fired. A scenario replays a way in, not an implementation: the binding chosen under the profile decides which graphs actually run.

policy.description: A policy this scenario replays instead of the trigger's fire: its `decide` is fired under the trigger's kind and settings, the way `wilanis rehearse` walks a policy's decision. The trigger must attach it (S005).

branch.description: The decision this scenario proves: the graph that declares the switch, the switch's node id, the rule's expression (`else` for the else), and the node the rule routes to. `wilanis regress` names it first when the run differs; `wilanis check` refuses one the tree no longer has (S004).

graph.description: The graph that declares the switch.

node.description: The id of the switch node whose rule this scenario takes.

when.description: The rule's expression as the graph writes it, or `else` for the else.

to.description: The node the rule routes to.

seed.description: The seed wilanis fuzz generated this run's input from, so the same input can be generated again.

in.description: The input the trigger was fired with, generated from the seed and recorded as it was.

request.description: The request the run read, for a trigger whose kind hands one; what fire.in and any policy read from.

stubs.description: dotted node path -> the value its operation returned.

cancelAt.description: The dotted node path of one stubbed effect at which the replay cancels the run: wilanis regress aborts the run's signal when that node is reached, and the node rejects the way an aborted call does. Must be a key of stubs. wilanis fuzz never writes it; an author does, to pin a deadline.

expect.description: The report this run produced, which wilanis regress replays against and diffs node by node.

status.description: How the run as a whole ended: done; failed (a refusal -- the graph's, a policy's or the guard's -- or a fault); blocked (a root it reads was never supplied); cancelled (its signal fired before it finished); or unreachable (the solver could reach no input for the scenario's branch, so nothing ran and `unreachable` says why).

output.description: What the run answered, recorded as it was.

reason.description: For a run that failed at a refuse node the graph declares, its reason (`refusalOf`), so a replay says when the declared outcome changed and not only that a node did.

unreachable.description: Why the solver could reach no input for this branch, in its words. Present exactly when `status` is `unreachable`; the scenario then has no `in` and no `stubs`, and `regress` re-solves instead of running.

nodes.description: What each node did, by its dotted path, so a replay says which node first differs.

handler.description: For a call or a map, the operation that ran, so a replay says when a node was rebound rather than only that its answer changed.

out.description: What this node answered, recorded as it was.

selected.description: For a switch, the rule it took, so a replay says when routing changed.

reason.description: For a node that refused on purpose, the reason it gave; absent for a node that answered or broke. A replay whose reason differs, or whose refusal became a fault, is a diff.

if.description: `status` says whether the solver reached the branch, so `unreachable` goes with the one status that says it did not.

status.description: Selects the expectation of a branch no input reaches.

then.description: A branch no input reaches: why, in the solver's words.

else.description: A run that happened: its nodes say what it did, and nothing is left unreachable to explain.
